driver: A period total counts each scheduled payment in the period it is actually released, payments due on a non-business day are released on the next business day by a rule only the payment history shows, and every closed period ended on a business day, so the closed totals confirm a count by scheduled date exactly; the forward period ends on a weekend, so the payments due that day fall into the next period, while a capped line whose claims always stayed under its cap now carries claims, grossed up from the share received by the decision date, that exceed it.
driver_concrete: FY2029 state financial support for special education is counted by release date; formula aid installment 12, the second half of transportation aid and the June state schools allotment are due Saturday 30 June 2029 and are released on Monday 2 July under the next-business-day rule that every weekend and holiday date in three closed years and FY2029 to date shows, so they land in FY2030, while 30 June was a business day in every closed year; and high-cost reimbursements, paid in full in every closed year, are limited to the categorical balance left after full-year transportation aid and the state schools' allotments once the claims received by mid-January are grossed up by the share every closed year had received by that date.
stump: A competent solver rebuilds FY2029 support line by line from the payment schedule, the December 2028 child count and the high-cost claims, ties every certified closed-year total to the dollar, and files a supplemental near zero; it books the 30 June 2029 payments in FY2029 although that day is a Saturday and the history releases such payments on the next business day, and it pays the high-cost line at its claims trend although the grossed-up claims exceed the appropriation, so FY2029 support falls tens of millions short of FY2028.
notes: Drawn 2026-10-03 after the advisor's two-insight rule: the roll is unfiled (pinned by payment-history identity), the cap is a quantity predicate (claims grossed up against an appropriation). Decisive generator G13 (which period a release falls in) because task105 holds G7. Gate G forecasting repeats task105 (WARN, answered in the design note).
